content:
As mentioned here: #mathlib4 > shake @ 💬, I've been trying to shake Mathlib wjile allowing shake to demote public to private imports. TL;DR: shake is not up to it yet.

After a few false starts, I added -- shake: keep-all to all deprecated modules and all Mathlib.Tactic modules; then I ran shake --keep-implied --keep-prefix --fix on Mathlib, fixed the errors, built again, ... After repeating this cycle for about a dozen times, I decided that at this point, continuing would be a waste of time.

There are a number of different kinds of errors (a more detailed analysis will follow eventually):

  • shake seems to be over-zealous in demoting from public to private imports. There are many instances when a declaration that is imported privately is needed in the public scope.
  • There are cases where it appears certain (basic) declarations are not imported at all.
  • In many cases, an import of Mathlib.Tactic.FBinop was missing.
  • The deriving handler for Fintype does no longer work.

In some (or even many) cases, the error message is informative and tells me what I should add as public import. But there are also many cases where the error one gets is rather obscure, e.g., when using dot notation, or I'm told that a certain instance cannot be synthesized, but without information what I need to add for it to succeed.

I have put together a collection of error messages (in a not very systematic way), which I will post here tomorrow.

For now, I'll just give you a teaser:

error: failed to synthesize instance of type class
  failed to pretty print expression (use 'set_option pp.rawOnError true' for raw representation)

Hint: Type class instance resolution failures can be inspected with the `set_option trace.Meta.synthInstance true` command.
You can have a look at #39386 to see what the fixes look like.
See Bryan's comments here #mathlib4 > shake @ 💬 and my comments before and after, to see the problems I had when I shook FLT and then tried to fix things.

Let me try to structure my findings a bit.

The first point I want to raise is the observation that shake frequently demotes public imports to imports even though some declartions from the imported module are needed in the public scope. My gut feeling is that this may be related (in many cases, at least) with the fact (?) that proof fields in public structures are exposed. (To see this, I've set up a simple test project (without Mathlib), as follows:

ShakeTest/Defs.lean:

module

/-!
# Define a constant for downstream use
-/

@[expose] public section

def mystery : Nat := 37

end

ShakeTest/Basic.lean:

module

public import ShakeTest.Defs

@[expose] public section

/-!
# Define a structure
-/

structure wrap where
  foo : Nat
  foo_eq : foo = 37

end

ShakeTest/Lemmas.lean:

module

public import ShakeTest.Defs

/-!
# A lemma
-/

@[expose] public section

theorem mystery_eq : mystery = 37 := rfl

end

ShakeTest/Test.lean:

module

public import ShakeTest.Basic
public import ShakeTest.Lemmas

@[expose] public section

theorem bar : mystery = 37 := mystery_eq

def bang : wrap where
  foo := mystery
  foo_eq := mystery_eq

end

If you remove public from public import ShakeTest.Lemmas in the last file, you get an error on the second use of mystery_eq, but not on the first one.

module

public import ShakeTest.Basic
import ShakeTest.Lemmas

@[expose] public section

theorem bar : mystery = 37 := mystery_eq

/--
error: Unknown identifier `mystery_eq`

Note: A public declaration `mystery_eq` exists but is imported privately; consider adding `public import ShakeTest.Lemmas`.
-/
#guard_msgs in
def bang : wrap where
  foo := mystery
  foo_eq := mystery_eq

end

This looks like a bug in the module system to me: I would expect that all proofs are not exposed by default, even in an @[expose] public section.

Anyway, many of the failures I noticed removed something from the public scope, which is used in proof fields of structures. (Examples in the next message.) However, when I tried to check shake on my simple example above, it correctly says

  note: `public import ShakeTest.Lemmas` required
    because `bang` refers to `mystery_eq`

so it is not clear to me what exactly goes wrong.

Here are some of the examples where I had to add public back.

-- ### Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.Subsemiring.Order

/--
error: Unknown identifier `mul_nonneg`

Note: A public declaration `mul_nonneg` exists but is imported privately; consider adding `public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.GroupWithZero.Unbundled.Basic`.
-/
#guard_msgs in
variable (R) in
/-- The set of nonnegative elements in an ordered semiring, as a subsemiring. -/
@[simps]
def nonneg : Subsemiring R where
  __ := AddSubmonoid.nonneg R
  mul_mem' := mul_nonneg
  one_mem' := zero_le_one

-- ### Mathlib.Order.ScottContinuity

-- error on `to_fun`
/--
error: Unknown constant `Set.image_congr`

Note: A public declaration `image_congr` exists but is imported privately; consider adding `public import Mathlib.Data.Set.Image`.
-/
#guard_msgs in
@[fun_prop, to_fun]
theorem ScottContinuousOn.comp {g : β → γ} {D'}
    (hD : ∀ a b : α, a ≤ b → {a, b} ∈ D) (hD' : Set.MapsTo (f '' ·) D D')
    (hg : ScottContinuousOn D' g) (hf : ScottContinuousOn D f) :
    ScottContinuousOn D (g ∘ f) := by
  intro d hd₁ hd₂ hd₃ a ha
  have hd : DirectedOn (fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 ≤ x2) (f '' d) := by
    have := hf.monotone
    simp only [Monotone, DirectedOn, mem_image, exists_exists_and_eq_and, forall_exists_index,
      and_imp, forall_apply_eq_imp_iff₂] at ⊢ this hd₃
    grind
  rw [Set.image_comp]
  exact hg (hD' hd₁) ⟨f hd₂.choose, by grind⟩ hd (hf hd₁ hd₂ hd₃ ha)

-- ### Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Field.Canonical

public section

variable {α : Type*} [Semifield α] [LinearOrder α] [CanonicallyOrderedAdd α]

/--
error: Unknown constant `PosMulReflectLT.toPosMulStrictMono`

Note: A public declaration `PosMulReflectLT.toPosMulStrictMono` exists but is imported privately; consider adding `public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.GroupWithZero.Unbundled.Basic`.
-/
#guard_msgs in
-- See note [reducible non-instances]
/-- Construct a `LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero` from a canonically linear ordered semifield. -/
abbrev CanonicallyOrderedAdd.toLinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero :
    LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero α where
  bot := 0
  bot_le _ := zero_le
  isBot_zero _ := zero_le
  mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left _a ha _b _c hbc :=
    have : PosMulStrictMono α := PosMulReflectLT.toPosMulStrictMono _
    mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hbc ha

-- ### Mathlib.Data.Finset.Attach

@[expose] public section

-- (...)

/--
error: Unknown identifier `nodup_attach`

Note: A public declaration `nodup_attach` exists but is imported privately; consider adding `public import Mathlib.Data.Multiset.MapFold`.
-/
#guard_msgs in
/-- `attach s` takes the elements of `s` and forms a new set of elements of the subtype
`{x // x ∈ s}`. -/
def attach (s : Finset α) : Finset { x // x ∈ s } :=
  ⟨Multiset.attach s.1, nodup_attach.2 s.2⟩

-- ### Mathlib.Order.Preorder.Chain

/--
error: Invalid field `symm_image_image`: The environment does not contain `RelIso.symm_image_image`, so it is not possible to project the field `symm_image_image` from an expression
  e
of type
  (fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 ≤ x2) ≃r fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 ≤ x2
---
error: Invalid field `image_symm_image`: The environment does not contain `RelIso.image_symm_image`, so it is not possible to project the field `image_symm_image` from an expression
  e
of type
  (fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 ≤ x2) ≃r fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 ≤ x2
-/
#guard_msgs in
/-- Flags are preserved under order isomorphisms. -/
def map (e : α ≃o β) : Flag α ≃ Flag β where
  toFun s := ofIsMaxChain _ (s.maxChain.image e)
  invFun s := ofIsMaxChain _ (s.maxChain.image e.symm)
  left_inv s := ext <| e.symm_image_image s
  right_inv s := ext <| e.image_symm_image s

-- Solution: make `import Mathlib.Order.Hom.Set` public.
-- (There is OrderIso.symm_image_image etc.; OrderIso is an abbrev for RelIso with LE.le)

There are actually two issues here. One is the problem with shake and the other one is that in some of these cases, the error messages are rather obscure. This occurs

  • when dot notation is involved (as in the last example in my previous message). Here it would be helpful if (in the example) it could be checked whether OrderIso.symm_image_image is available in the private scope before unfolding to RelIso. (But, of course, the proof fields where this occurs should be private anyway IMO.)
  • when instance synthesis is involved. It would be helpful if, when synthesis fails in the public scope, it could be run again in the private scope, so that a more helpful error message can be generated. I'll give some error examples in the next message.

-- ### Mathlib.Data.Vector.Basic

/--
error: failed to synthesize instance of type class
  IsRightCancelAdd ℕ

Hint: Type class instance resolution failures can be inspected with the `set_option trace.Meta.synthInstance true` command.
-/
#guard_msgs in
/--
Define `C v` by induction on `v : Vector α n`.

This function has two arguments: `nil` handles the base case on `C nil`,
and `cons` defines the inductive step using `∀ x : α, C w → C (x ::ᵥ w)`.

It is used as the default induction principle for the `induction` tactic.
-/
@[elab_as_elim, induction_eliminator]
def inductionOn {C : ∀ {n : ℕ}, Vector α n → Sort*} {n : ℕ} (v : Vector α n)
    (nil : C nil) (cons : ∀ {n : ℕ} {x : α} {w : Vector α n}, C w → C (x ::ᵥ w)) : C v := by
  induction n with
  | zero =>
    rcases v with ⟨_ | ⟨-, -⟩, - | -⟩
    exact nil
  | succ n ih =>
    rcases v with ⟨_ | ⟨a, v⟩, v_property⟩
    cases v_property
    exact cons (ih ⟨v, (add_left_inj 1).mp v_property⟩)

-- Solution: add `public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Group.Nat`.

-- ### Mathlib.Data.PNat.Factors

@[expose] public section

/--
error: failed to synthesize instance of type class
  IsOrderedCancelAddMonoid (Multiset Nat.Primes)

Hint: Type class instance resolution failures can be inspected with the `set_option trace.Meta.synthInstance true` command.
---
error: Failed to delta derive `IsOrderedCancelAddMonoid` instance for `PrimeMultiset`.

Note: Delta deriving tries the following strategies: (1) inserting the definition into each explicit non-out-param parameter of a class and (2) unfolding definitions further.
---
error: failed to synthesize instance of type class
  CanonicallyOrderedAdd (Multiset Nat.Primes)

Hint: Type class instance resolution failures can be inspected with the `set_option trace.Meta.synthInstance true` command.
---
error: Failed to delta derive `CanonicallyOrderedAdd` instance for `PrimeMultiset`.

Note: Delta deriving tries the following strategies: (1) inserting the definition into each explicit non-out-param parameter of a class and (2) unfolding definitions further.
-/
#guard_msgs in
/-- The type of multisets of prime numbers.  Unique factorization
gives an equivalence between this set and ℕ+, as we will formalize
below. -/
def PrimeMultiset :=
  Multiset Nat.Primes
deriving Inhabited, AddCommMonoid, SemilatticeSup, DistribLattice,
  Sub, IsOrderedCancelAddMonoid, CanonicallyOrderedAdd, OrderBot, OrderedSub

-- Solution: make `import Mathlib.Data.Multiset.OrderedMonoid` public.

A frequent error was error: elaboration function for `FBinopElab.prodSyntax` has not been implemented, which can be resolved by importing Mathlib.Tactic.FBinop. I assume that shake will be unable in principle to notice this, because this concerns elaboration, and what is in the .olean file does not keep a trace of what was needed during elaboration (I may be wrong, though; I'm not an expert on this).

The remedy here should be to add a few well-considered shake: keep annotations to make sure that this module is (publicly and transitively) imported in basically all of Mathlib.

Another interesting failure was that the deriving handler for Fintype did no longer work. The error looks like this.

-- ### Mathlib.Data.Sign.Defs

@[expose] public section

/-- error: Unknown constant `List.Nodup.of_map` -/
#guard_msgs in
-- Don't generate unnecessary `sizeOf_spec` lemmas which the `simpNF` linter will complain about.
set_option genSizeOfSpec false in
/-- The type of signs. -/
inductive SignType
  | zero
  | neg
  | pos
  deriving DecidableEq, Inhabited, Fintype

-- Error is on `Fintype` and persists
-- even after adding `public` to `import Mathlib.Data.List.Nodup`;
-- `#check List.Nodup.of_map` immediately before verifies this exists.

The strange thing is that even after publicly importing the declaration it complains about, the error still persists.

And now here is a strange one. After shakeing (and some rounds of fixing),

So declarations that were not visible before now suddely are. Which must mean that the changes made by shake actually have added some transitive imports that had not been there before. Which seems to run pretty clearly against its specification. I should say that this may have been caused by some of the fixes I made in upstream files, but I am fairly certain that these should only have added back (public) imports that had been there before.

Here is another case of an unhelpful dot notation related error message.

-- ### Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.Subring.Units

/-- error: Unknown constant `Units.inv_pos.mpr` -/
#guard_msgs in
/-- The subgroup of positive units of a linear ordered semiring. -/
def Units.posSubgroup (R : Type*) [Semiring R] [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] :
    Subgroup Rˣ :=
  { (Submonoid.pos R).comap (Units.coeHom R) with
    carrier := { x | (0 : R) < x }
    inv_mem' := Units.inv_pos.mpr }

Here it should check if Units.inv_pos is available in the private scope.

Finally, the strangest thing I encountered was that at some point in the process, there was a file (Mathlib/Order/Monotone/Extension.lean) that compiled just fine in VSCode, but gave an error when running lake build on it. How am I supposed to fix the problem if it is not even present when I'm looking at the file?

Here is a small test I jsut did. On current master, run lake shake --explain Mathlib.Data.List.Pairwise and then replace the imports (of only that file) with what shake suggests. This gives (in that file, around line 120)

/-! ### Pairwise filtering -/

/-- error: Unknown constant `pwFilter_eq_self` -/
#guard_msgs in
protected alias ⟨_, Pairwise.pwFilter⟩ := pwFilter_eq_self

(which can be fixed by adding public back to import Batteries.Data.List.Pairwise).

Thanks for doing this, that's a good to-do list :smile: . I'll have to go through them one-by-one but a preliminary response:

  • It should be feasible to improve all these error messages, yes!
  • On the other hand, it is likely not feasible to switch to the private scope whenever entering a subterm of prop type, which would be the correct fix for the proof issues you found - i.e. this is a module system limitation, not shake's per se. Currently this is decided purely syntactically, which makes it predictable: theorem bodies and by do this transfer. Thus by exact is always available as a workaround that does not require bumping imports. Having said that, the special case of entering proof fields is likely so common and "syntactic enough" that I'll probably go ahead and implement the transfer for it.

Sebastian Ullrich said:

  • it is likely not feasible to switch to the private scope whenever entering a subterm of prop type, which would be the correct fix for the proof issues

Why would that be not feasible? (I have no idea how this is implemented, so I'm asking out of curiosity.)

Because due to metavariables, it is not even clear at what point it is known for a subterm to be a proof. This is not an issue for by as its elaboration is delayed anyway. And it is unlikely to be an issue in practice for fields.

• lean4#13751 is the proof fields change
  • batteries#1808 fixes alias
  • lean4#13752 fixes the projection error message

Michael Stoll said:

A frequent error was error: elaboration function for `FBinopElab.prodSyntax` has not been implemented, which can be resolved by importing Mathlib.Tactic.FBinop. I assume that shake will be unable in principle to notice this, because this concerns elaboration, and what is in the .olean file does not keep a trace of what was needed during elaboration (I may be wrong, though; I'm not an expert on this).

The remedy here should be to add a few well-considered shake: keep annotations to make sure that this module is (publicly and transitively) imported in basically all of Mathlib.

Half of the new shake is all about recording elaboration requirements but when it comes to the definition of elaborators, it cannot foresee what requirements running that elaborator will have. What this means in this case is that any macro (an elaborator special case) that uses fbinop% in its right-hand side must ensure FBinop is imported publicly and not shaken away. You will find many existing -- shake: keep ([...] dependency) that do this.

So to summarize: the syntax used in a macro should be imported publicly once in the macro's module, not at each use site of the macro
Now while arbitrary elaborators are very much unpredictable, we could probably automate something here in this special case of macros

BTW, is it possible to runshake just on one module (and not also on its transitive dependencies)? I think this would help quite a bit when experimenting. The --help text does not seem to list a suitable option.
--only mentioned above should do this

lake shake --explain Mathlib.Data.List.Defs works as advertised.

Here is a question. I had assumed that adding module -- shake: keep-downstream would make shake not touch downstream imports of the module that contains this line. But in an experimental branch, I have added -- shake: keep-downstream to Mathlib.Tactic.FBinop, and running lake shake --explain Mathlib.Data.List.Defsshows the lines

/home/mstoll/lean4/mathlib4/Mathlib/Data/SProd.lean:
  remove #[public import Mathlib.Tactic.FBinop]
  add #[import Mathlib.Tactic.FBinop]

so shake would remove the public label on the import, which is what I wanted to avoid.

Also,

  remove #[public import Mathlib.Util.CompileInductive, public import Batteries.Tactic.Lint.Basic, public import Batteries.Logic]

so shake would then add import Mathlib.Tactic.FBimop to essentially all downstream files, which should be avoided if the import remained public in Mathlib.Data.SProd.
Hmm the current assumption is that keep-downstream adheres to whether --add-public is used. But why do you not want to use keep here?

Maybe the better question is the following. Can I make sure in some way that all downstream modules that currently import a given module publicly (maybe indirectly) keep doing that when running shake (without `--add-public' )?
I don't think there is a way currently except to mark all of them as keep. We could certainly add a keep-downstream variant but I would like to understand the use case first
Say, to make sure that notation/elaboration dependencies are available that shake may not be able to track? (And without importing these explicitly in all modules.)

You put keep on the import in the elaborator's module. This is the correct, precise solution.

module
public import Mathlib.Tactic.FBinop  -- shake: keep (macro output dependency)

[...]

macro_rules | `($x ×ˢ $y)   => `(fbinop% SProd.sprod $x $y)
This ensures the import is always at least as visible as the macro
Does this work for modules transitively importing the one containing this line?
Either they (transitively) import this module, so by this it's guaranteed they will import FBinop as well, or they don't so it doesn't matter

OK; I'll see if it works.

Ah, this is good info to put in the future docstring... --only will still visit modules upstream and downstream of the given module and see if it has to add new imports to them - ideally this should never be necessary upstream but can be necessary downstream. The overall context of the shake is given by the optional flag-less argument, like you used in lake shake --explain Mathlib.Data.List.Defs. So if you don't want shake to attempt to fix downstream modules, lake shake Mathlib.Data.List.Defs --only Mathlib.Data.List.Defs should do it
So basically shake should only touch files in the intersection of the upwards closure of the first module and the downwards closure of the second one when used in this way
(and then intersected with the current package, it does not touch upstream dependencies)

I just ran lake shake --explain Mathlib.Data.List.Defs --only Mathlib.Data.List.Defs, but it still lists proposed import changes for the upstream files (starting with Mathlib/Tactic/Linter/DirectoryDependency.lean). I would have expected to see only the one file in the intersection in the output.
Then that's either a known or unknown shake issue :)

Comparing with the output without --only ..., the proposed changes are somewhat different.
Still, what I would like to see is changes only made to what is in the intersection.

If I understand correctly, then shake checks that everything it looks at builds (by checking that the oleans are up to date). So it should never be necessary to add (or upgrade) imports in files it is not supposed to touch.

Here is another issue. It looks like shake by default runs lake build --no-build on the full tree, not restricted to the modules it is supposed to work on (and their dependencies). This is annoying when I want to work my way from the root to the leaves, as making modifications near the root will invalidate a lot of downstream oleans.
